questions.question: Day 15 Practice (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)): When talking about giving street directions (right now), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'The cab driver'?

options.a: Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.
options.b: Signal crossing left turn take. yesterday
options.c: Signal crossing left turn take.
options.d: I am giving street directions right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Take a left turn after crossing the traffic signal.".

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'fill out'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: Complete an official form.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'fill out' means: complete an official form. Example: "Please fill out this registration form."

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'pick out'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Carefully choose specific items from a group.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'pick out' means: carefully choose specific items from a group. Example: "Could you help me pick out the best mangos?"

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 1 (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "నాకు కొంచెం తలనొప్పిగా ఉంది, ఒక గంట సేపు రెస్ట్ తీసుకుంటాను."
(Literal attempt: "To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.")

options.a: I am needing to to me little headache is there, take rest one hour.
options.b: I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: To me little headache is there, take rest one hour.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I have a slight headache; I'm going to rest for an hour."

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 2 (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "నా పార్సెల్ ఈ రోజు సాయంత్రానికి డెలివరీ అవుతుందా?"
(Literal attempt: "My parcel today evening delivery becoming?")

options.a: My parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to my parcel today evening delivery becoming?
options.d: Will my package be delivered by this evening?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "Will my package be delivered by this evening?"

Use 'Will my package be delivered...' for delivery tracking.

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 3 (Workplace Standups & Agendas (Phase 3)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.d: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
